entry_exit_instruction.reachability: Not established: normal cleanup exits before its trailing ret and the startup epilogue.

address_domains: Separate FWSEC/PRE_OS IMEM VAs; engine-object/source/stack are synthetic local DMEM. PRI operands and Falcon IO ports are distinct. Destination 0x1c comes from copied PRE_OS interface. Large PRE_OS D[0x140...] operands are not aliased to physical PRI.
limits: Interface walk is a file parser cross-checked against retained instructions; upstream firmware load/PIO reads are unexecuted. Writer executes copied control code with synthetic PRI and IO adapters. Capacity 4096 and transport completion/status are fixtures. IO writes are event records, not physical bus emulation. DMEM reconstruction uses documented auto-increment semantics, not observed GPU memory. Callback dispatch stops at first nontrivial init/exit targets; no whole callback sequence completes. A separate bit-6 consumer reaches unexecuted 0x1484; its continuation cases supply explicitly synthetic service returns. Return fragments start after the unexecuted exit callbacks and stop before crypto cleanup. A separate integer-register clearing tail reaches the cleanup exit; crypto, IO and cauth operations before that tail remain unexecuted. The normal copied cleanup exits before returning to the startup epilogue. No whole boot, installed-ROM identity, debug/production equivalence, outage diagnosis, actual HALTED result or recovery method is proven.
